art.subject: Ferruginous Flycatcher (Muscicapa ferruginea), adult (sexes alike), a spring migrant in Korean island woodland: head slate-grey, contrasting with the brown back, with a prominent white eye-ring; throat white; mantle and back warm brown, becoming bright rufous on the rump and uppertail coverts; wings dark brown with rufous fringes to the greater coverts and tertials, forming a rufous wing bar; breast and flanks orange-rufous, centre of the belly whitish, undertail coverts rufous-buff; tail rufous-brown. Bill short and dark; eye large and dark.
art.pose: perched upright on a shaded branch below the canopy, side view
art.scene: shady mixed woodland on a Korean offshore island during spring migration (May), dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright on a shaded branch: rounded slate-grey head with a big dark eye and a white eye-ring, short dark bill with a pale base to the lower mandible, brown back, dark brown wings with rufous fringes to the coverts and tertials, rufous-orange breast and flanks, rufous rump, uppertail coverts and square tail, pinkish legs
adult, front three-quarter view perched upright: slate-grey head with a white eye-ring, pale throat, rufous-orange breast and flanks, rufous tail showing below the perch, pinkish legs
art.build: Small flycatcher, smaller than a sparrow, with a large rounded head, big dark eye and short neck; perches upright and still under the canopy and sallies out after insects. Bill short, flat and broad-based, much shorter than the head. Legs short and thin. Wings long, the primaries projecting well beyond the tertials. Tail medium length, square-ended, rufous, without white.
avoid: Do not paint a brown or grey-brown head; the head is clearly slate-grey, contrasting with the brown back.
Do not streak the breast like Grey-streaked Flycatcher; the breast is plain orange-rufous.
Do not paint a white wing patch or white tail sides (Ficedula flycatchers).
Do not make the rump and tail grey; they are bright rufous.
